title: Acquire
description: Keeps leads, notes, drafts, follow-ups, and submission records in one local workflow, so work opportunities do not slip between tools.
seoTitle: Acquire Case Study | Local-First Acquisition Operating System
seoDescription: How Acquire keeps sourcing, review, application drafts, submissions, outreach, and opportunity tracking in one local workflow.
constraints: The system had to stay local-first because it manages sensitive sourcing, application, resume, and outreach data.
Automation needed explicit approval gates, durable evidence, and recoverable jobs instead of hidden background actions.
problem: Finding and pursuing work was spread across job boards, LinkedIn, Upwork, recruiters, notes, browser tabs, emails, and manual follow-up lists.

The hard part was not just discovering more opportunities. It was deciding which opportunities were worth acting on, preparing the right materials, answering portal questions consistently, and knowing what was blocked or ready.
solution: Built a local command-line tool and database for opportunities, research runs, review queues, applications, outreach drafts, reusable answers, evidence timelines, reports, and scheduled jobs.
Added a native macOS workspace so daily work happens in Today, Reviews, Pursuits, Sources, and Settings instead of scattered terminal commands.
Used Codex and Playwriter behind explicit workflow boundaries: research and scoring produce inspectable records, draft generation requires review, and final submissions run only from approved inputs.
result: Turned a fragile acquisition process into a real operating system with source monitoring, review queues, application workflows, answer reuse, evidence timelines, and submission status in one place.

Separated judgment-heavy agent tasks from workflow ownership: the application owns state, queues, validation, and reports while agents produce research for a defined question, drafts, and browser evidence.
Created a reusable pattern for business systems engineering: map the operating workflow, define approval gates, store durable evidence, and build an interface that makes the next action obvious.
